answer: Proof-of-space curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to commit unique cryptographic tables to physical storage. An attacker cannot deploy zero-cost replicas, incurring the verifiable cost of dedicated drive capacity per identity. Even when tracking jade shipments or a coastal zephyr near an active harbor, nodes must answer rapid retrieval challenges. However, frequent read audits accelerate hardware wear and economically favor centralized storage cartels.
